chapters.html:
Phainon leaned against the wall beside the vending machine with a sigh, his eyes dry and crusty from keeping them wide open and focused for the gruelling and long surgery he'd just come out of. He was still in his scrubs, his white coat slung over a shoulder, contemplating if he should just sleep, scrubs and all as soon as he came home.

Of course that's not something he would do, it was a tempting thought nonetheless. 

He was snapped out of his thoughts when he heard a gruff voice hiss a curse, his eyes falling upon a Man looking at a can of fallen juice with frustration clearly seen in his pretty features and clenched fists that looked to be caused by something more than spilt juice. He also looked to be—

Phainon glanced at his midriff, keeping it brief to not be rude. 

The man looked to be about four months pregnant. He looked like he wanted to bend but hesitated every time he tried, prompting Phainon to walk up to him, pick the can up and put it in the trash for him after the fourth attempt. 

He turned to the man again not expecting to see a fierce frown directed his way. He cleared his throat and adjusted his skewed glasses, hoping his smile didn't look too tired. 

“Here by yourself?” He asked, only for the frown to turn even more fierce. 

“...I don't see why you need to know, Doctor.” the man said, his eyes narrowed in suspicion. Phainon raised his arms up in surrender, his chuckle a little awkward. The pregnant stranger was pretty, his features gorgeous despite his fierce frown. 

The man had wild blonde hair that resembled a lion's mane, the golden bleeding to red at the tips with a braid framing one side of his face. The face in question was breathtakingly beautiful, somehow both handsome and pretty with the sharp cut of his jaw and nose, slanted feline eyes with irises that burned like embers and framed by thick lashes that fluttered every time he blinked, lips soft and plush. 

His body was…something else. 

Now, Phainon was not a pervert. He was a well respected surgeon with many successful operations under his belt, a polite man who'd help your neighborhood grandmother cross the street. 

But by the titans. 

He was built like a warrior from the past, with broad shoulders and biceps that looked large even in his loose black shirt. His thighs looked strong, stretching his maternity pants with their girth. He didn’t let his eyes linger long, not wanting the man to think he was some depraved fool. But from what he'd managed to see, the soft curve of his heavy chest and the swell of his baby bump paired with his physique only made him look even more gorgeous, the pregnancy glow making him look almost ethereal. 

He cleared his throat, realizing the pause after the man spoke had gone on for a bit too long. 

“I…hope I didn't come across as rude. If I did, I apologize, that was not my intention…but I noticed you looked rather frustrated and I'd feel really bad if I didn't even offer a helping hand.” 

Phainon said, rubbing the back of his neck and hoping he didn’t look like a loser with his probably skewed glasses, mussed up hair and tired eyes. The man crossed his arms, waiting for Phainon to continue. 

“...Are you…by any chance, lost?” 

The man's pretty feline eyes widened in surprise before he looked away, a light pink dusting his cheeks. His partner is so lucky, Phainon couldn’t help but think, an irrational burst of jealousy making itself known in his gut.

“...was it that obvious?” the man muttered with a sigh, uncrossing his arms to pinch the bridge of his nose. 

“It wasn't really, just a lucky guess.” Phainon said with a breathy chuckle. 

“Visiting the ob-gyn?” He asked, adjusting the frames of his glasses. The man studied him for a moment before nodding. 

“I could…show you the way… if you don't mind, that is.” He heard himself offer, his mouth speaking words without consulting his brain. Logically, he should just point the man to the department and be on his way home and pass out on his bed after a scalding shower. But the way the man looked at him in a mix of surprise and gratefulness made him think he made the right decision. 

“...You don't have to but I appreciate the help, thank you.” The man said, his smile small and reserved but by the titans, it made him look so pretty. Phainon dumbly nodded in response, making sure he walked beside the man rather than in front when he was leading the way just in case he fell even if it wasn’t very likely because he's well aware of the consequences when a baby is involved. 

The silence was awkward, only their steady footsteps accompanying them to the lift lobby. Phainon struggled to find a topic he could talk to the man about without accidentally pushing a button he didn't mean to. Pregnancy was a very sensitive topic and he wasn’t sure he was prepared to avoid landmines after having completed a surgery that took about six hours because of an unprecedented complication. He sighed, remembering the blood vessel that exploded right when they'd almost been done, the operation room erupting in a cacophony of beeping from the machines and the spilling of blood in places where it shouldn’t be. 

His sigh must have been too weary and heavy because the one who broke their silence was the standoffish blonde. 

“...Did you just finish your shift?” He asked, his brows furrowed. They'd made it to the lift lobby which was thankfully empty. It was around 10am, he should have been home at 6. Phainon laughed tiredly, leading the man into the lift before hitting the button to take them to the gynecology floor. 

“Ah…it ran a little late, should have been done a few hours ago but you know how it goes…patient's femoral artery explodes and splatters my coworker in blood and then we got to make sure the said patient doesn't die.” 

He said with a tired shrug. The man looked a little concerned. 

“Oh don't worry about the patient, he lived to see another day! Had to stay a while to see if he was stabilized enough before I could clock off,” Phainon continued, belatedly realizing he was rambling about his day to a pretty man he barely knew. He cleared his throat, looking straight ahead at the lift doors opening to the gynecology floor. 

“Taking me to the ob-gyn must have been an inconvenience, are you sure—” 

“Oh no! Not at all. It's a nice change of pace actually. Worked in this hospital for about 3 years and I've only visited the gynecology floor a handful of times.” He assured the pregnant man with a shake of his head. The man frowned, his mouth opening and closing wordlessly before he sighed. 

“I owe you one, Doctor.” He said with a gruffly, the severe clench of his jaw a little softened now, no longer donning an expression akin to a standoffish stray cat. Phainon smiled, waving a hand dismissively. 

“You don't owe me anything! I'm glad I got to help—” He was interrupted by a flurry of movement that happened all at once. 

A man had bumped into a nurse who in turn bumped into a janitor who'd been dragging a cleaning trolley with them, who in turn dropped their cleaning supplies that just happened to be in the path of a man who is very clearly pregnant. He had only a few seconds to react, so he just did the best thing he could do. 

He spun the blonde haired man out of the way and held him close, placing a steadying hand on the small of his back. The whole thing felt too corny like those hallmark movies Castorice seemed to like but Phainon didn’t have the mental capacity to linger on that, too distracted by the gorgeous man in his arms. 

He was so close, his golden eyes wide with surprise. He was clinging to Phainon’s shoulders, his nails digging into his scrubs. He was breathtakingly gorgeous. This close, he could see that his eyelashes were dark and long, fluttering every time he blinked, his golden eyes flecked with orange looking very much like a sunburst. And by the titans, his lips. His plump lower lip had a dip in the middle almost as if it was beckoning Phainon to bite and lick it. He swallowed, his fingers flexing on the small of the man’s back. He smelt so good, like Pomegranates and something mellow and sweet, the faint scent of milk—

A squeal broke him out of his increasingly concerning spiral of thoughts, his eyes snapping up to the woman in front of them with her hands on his mouth, her eyes sparkling with wonder. She was also in scrubs but she wore her white coat over it, her brown hair neatly tied up in a bun. 

“Doctor Khaslana! I didn't know you had a partner! Titans above, he looks so beautiful!” 

The two of them shared a wide eyed look, the blonde hair man's cheeks turning an alluring pink. 

“Uh,” Phainon began when the man he was holding remained silent. 

“When I saw you two in the hallway I was going to tell you guys that checkups that haven't already been booked were not going to be possible today because Dr. Hyacinthia is attending a conference but I can make an exception for you and your partner, Dr. Khaslana!” She gushed, cupping her hands over her cheeks now. 

Phainon heard the man in his arms inhale sharply. He cleared his throat, gently releasing the man even if he wanted to rip his hands away in embarrassment. 

“Dr. Clementine, I—” 

“—m so grateful, you have my thanks.” Phainon slowly turned his head to look at the man who hijacked his sentence. The blonde haired man refused to look his way, gazing straight ahead at Clementine who just happened to be one of the people Phainon was hoping to find. Not like this but he digresses. He choked when the man held his hand and leaned his head on his shoulder. 

The movement was stilted and awkward, the man's ears a bright red, his expression stiff and uncomfortable but somehow Clementine seemed convinced, giggling in delight. 

“Oh all our department girls are going to be so sad!” She said, sounding very delighted about that. Phainon laughed awkwardly, turning to face her again. He decided to play along for now, pretending to be the partner of a beautiful man wasn't necessarily a chore. 

Though he does feel like a homewrecker. 

“Haha…why would they be sad?” He asked, following her with the other man in a tow.

“The charming and handsome but surprisingly mysterious prince of the General Medicine department has a partner! Why wouldn't they be sad? They've been trying to shoot their shot with you for years!” 

Phainon almost tripped over his feet, saved by a firm hand around waist. 

“Thanks,” he murmured under his breath to the man beside him who still refused to meet his gaze. The blonde hair man simply nodded stiffly. 

“I…wasn't aware of that…haha,” Phainon said in response to Clementine's words, the amount of things happening a little too much for his tired brain. 

They'd finally reached the room that seemed to be the check up area for people who were expecting. 

“Ah, I understand, Doctor Khaslana. With a partner so beautiful it would be remiss to even consider the possibility of anyone trying to ask you out!” 

She said with a smile. Phainon blankly nodded, automatically smiling in response. What was even happening?! He thought to himself, a little hysterical. He felt a warm hand squeeze his, prompting him to look at the man beside him. He genuinely looked apologetic. 

“Thank you for taking me here,” he said softly. 

“...You should go home and rest. I'll make it up to you somehow.” 

Phainon shook his head with a smile. 

“I'll be waiting out here for you.” He said with a tired smile, gesturing to the seats behind him with a thumb. It would look rather weird if he left his…partner all alone and went home. 

He must have fallen asleep because the next thing he knew after taking a seat in the waiting area was being woken up by something cool against his cheek. He groaned, his heavy eyelids opening slowly. He straightened and adjusted his glasses, not managing to bite back his gasp of surprise when he saw the blonde hair man looking down at him and holding a can of chilled pomegranate milk. 

“I…wasn't sure what drink you'd like but I bought you a can of pomegranate milk. Let me know if that's not to your liking, I can get something else.” 

Phainon blinked, before scrambling to stand up, taking the can of pomegranate milk from the man. 

“Ah no! That's fine! I like Pomegranates.” He said with what he hoped was a reassuring smile. It took him a second to register that they were standing really…really close. He realized the man was a little shorter than him. He'd thought he was taller. They were close enough for Phainon to smell the man’s delectable scent again. And if he moved closer he'd—

He swallowed and took a step back. 

“How is the baby?” He asked, hoping the man didn’t notice him being weird. The blonde haired man blinked in surprise before a faint smile pulled at his plush lips. 

“The baby is very healthy…the pregnancy seems to be going well, thank you for asking.” 

His smile faded when he seemed to remember something, his expression morphing into one of shame.

“...Thank you for going along with my lie. I'm sorry for inconveniencing you. It's just that I—” 

“Hey no, don't worry about it! I just hope your…uh…actual partner doesn’t think I'm a home wrecker.” 

The man looked surprised, before he laughed, his eyes curving in amusement. 

“It's an IVF baby, I don't have a partner.” 

“Oh,” Phainon managed to say, the feeling of relief and oddly enough, elation was immediate. The man studied him for a moment, his smile turning teasing. 

“Were you hoping I was single, Doctor Khaslana?” 

Phainon choked, his skin burning with embarrassment and something else. He opened and closed his mouth like a fish. 

“I-I…uh—”

The man laughed again, the sound of it somehow so beautiful. Beautiful enough that he didn't care that he was laughing at him. 

“Cute,” he said softly, so soft that Phainon thinks that maybe he was hallucinating. 

“Thank you for today. Go home and get some rest, Doctor.” He said with a pretty smile, adjusting Phainon's glasses before he turned to leave. 

Phainon thinks he may have stood there, still as a statue for a concerning amount of time.

***

He didn’t think they'd meet again. 

Phainon was left to fend for his life to find a cafe near the hospital for his coffee fix since the coffee machine was broken. He’d managed to find a cafe that was just a block away, its charming exterior and the smell of freshly baked bread beckoning him like the call of a siren. He was greeted with a jingle when he opened the door, pleasantly surprised by the clean and simple interior, the space spruced up by the rustic chalk board with today’s specials and the cute murals of desserts and drinks on the walls. 

“Ah. We meet again, Doctor Khaslana.” A deep and very familiar voice said. Phainon narrowly stopped himself from jumping like a spooked small dog and turned to the counter to see a sight for sore eyes. The blonde haired man from a few days ago somehow looked even more gorgeous than the first time he’d seen him. His carmine tipped hair was tied up in a loose bun, his signature braid left loose by his cheek. He was dressed in a navy blue turtleneck and a pair of black maternity pants, the pink apron he wore over them highlighting the swell of his belly and had the words ‘Bun in the oven!’ embroidered in blue on it. Phainon was suddenly very short of breath. 

“Hey!” He croaked. He cringed, clearing his throat and trying again.

“Hey! I hope you’re doing well? Any nausea in the morning? Swelling of feet? Back pai–”

“I’m doing fine, don’t worry too much about it.” The man cut him off with an amused smile. 

“Here for your coffee fix? You look like you’re about to keel over.” The man said, saving Phainon the embarrassment of fumbling over his words again. He nodded, walking towards the counter. There were trays of decadent looking desserts in the display counter but nothing looked as alluring as the man leaning forward against the counter and smiling at Phainon from under his dark eyelashes. 

“The coffee machine in the break room exploded…it was a mess.” Phainon muttered with a weary sigh. 

“Ah! And please don’t call me Doctor Khaslana, Phainon’s just fine.”

The man cocked his head, resting his chin on a fist.

“Weird name but oddly cute. The name’s Mydeimos but you can call me Mydei.”

Phainon had blanked for a moment, the word cute echoing in his head before he forced himself to snap out of it. 

“...Mydeimos is a really regal name, you sound like a warrior prince.” He managed to say, hoping the pause wasn’t too pronounced. The man—Mydei, grinned, his canines sharp like a wild cat. His heavy bosom was pronounced with how it was pushed up against the counter. Phainon immediately peeled his eyes away from the swell of his chest. 

“A flatterer and a doctor. You must be really busy.” He said, straightening up and crossing his arms. The movement made the largeness of his chest even more pronounced. Phainon swallowed. 

“Very busy,” He said with a sigh. Mydei hummed in amusement.

“What would you like to have?” He asked, motioning with his chin towards the chalkboard.

“We have seasonal special desserts you can get with your coffee.”

“Ah that's fine! Just a black coffee please.” 

Mydei raised an eyebrow but got to work. Phainon immediately felt a pang of guilt. 

“I hope I’m not overworking you…I can have something prepackaged if that’s—”

“Calm down. I’m pregnant, not bedridden. Besides, there will be no prepackaged goods in my cafe.” 

Mydei huffed, expertly making his coffee and setting the steaming cup on a tray with a lemon square he’d been eyeing in the display case. 

“Sit here and have your coffee, you look tired. I’m sure your work can wait.” He said imperiously, taking the tray before Phainon even had the chance and walked around the counter to set it on a table, his sharp golden eyes challenging Phainon to do otherwise. 

“I haven't paid yet.” Phainon interjected meekly. 

“On the house. If I see you pull your card out I will snap it in half.” He warned, his voice low. 

Phainon chuckled, partly amused and partly flustered.

“You got it, boss…I’ve been meaning to ask but where are the other employees?”

“Sent them off for a break since we don’t get a lot of customers during this hour.” Mydei said with a shrug. 

“Would you like to join me then? I’d feel bad seeing you stand the whole time,” He said with a smile he hoped wasn’t too wobbly with nervousness, his palms sweaty. He wasn’t sure why but he wanted to spend more time with this man, wanted to know more about his likes and dislikes, wanted to hold him close and bury his face in his soft blonde hair wanted to—

He was snapped out of his delusional thoughts by the scrape of a chair and a sigh as Mydei sat down across him. 

“Is being a worrywart a doctor trait or is it special to you?”

“Haha…I’d say both…Talking about being a worrywart, since your sperm donor is a stranger, you should call up the place and ask for the person’s health records. Don’t worry about the legality of it, just mention my name.” Phainon heard himself speak before his brain caught up, cold sweat coating the back of his neck when Mydei gaped at him in confusion.

“...sorry?”

“Ah! I hope I’m not misstepping. It’s just that I have a contact—” The contact being his foster mother Aglaea, “—who works there!” She owns the only sperm bank in the city. She also owned the hospital he worked in.“And I just wanted you to be prepared for congenital disorders that could pass down from the father.” 

Mydei blinked slowly before a low rumble of a chuckle escaped him. He leaned forward on the table, resting his cheek on an open palm. 

“You’re a little weird but that’s cute. I’ll do that, thank you.” 

Phainon spluttered, his cheeks burning. Why did this man keep calling him cute?!

“I’m not cute! I’m telling you about the medical intricacies of pregnancy!”

Mydei smiled, taking a bite of his lemon square. 

“Go ahead, I’m not stopping you.”

Phainon didn’t realize he’d been so engrossed in the space the both of them created, the topic going from medicine to video games they both play, though it was mostly him speaking and Mydei humming as he kept his pretty golden eyes fixed on him. He jolted when his phone buzzed in his pocket, gasping when he saw that his colleague was calling and realized he was very late. 

He got up and shoved the rest of the lemon square in his mouth. 

“Theesh are good!” He said with a double thumbs up, belatedly realizing something else. He fished his phone out of his pocket again and handed it over to a confused Mydei. 

“...Can I have your number? J-just in case you need help at the hospital again!” 

His skin burned under Mydei’s studying stare, the slow stretch of his lips into an amused smile making him turn embarrassingly redder. 

“Mm, Sure. Make sure to come by here for your daily caffeine fix. Our coffee is better than the engine oil your coffee machine probably gives you.”

Ever since then, they’d met regularly in Mydei’s cafe. He’d always sit across Phainon and they’d share a conversation, sometimes they’d sit beside each other in silence or even play mobile games to pass the time. It was nice. He didn’t really know what they were. Friends didn’t seem to fit right and it’s not like they’ve kissed. 

Not that Phainon hasn’t thought about it. 

He can’t help it. Mydei is gorgeous. He willingly sits closer than what is deemed to be polite when he sits beside him, his feet tangling with Phainon’s when they sit across from each other. His smiles are sweet and his teasing makes Phainon burn with want, his small touches like stroking Phainon’s cheek or adjusting his glasses were so dizzyingly nice. 

Everyday felt good, amazing even despite how bleak his shifts at the hospital were sometimes. 

But something was different today. 

Phainon had missed their afternoon breaktime, showing up at 9pm instead, weary and numb. The surgery he just performed was…gruelling. He’d managed to save the patient somehow despite the near close call of death but they’d quickly fallen into a coma right after and nothing seemed to be working. He’d been obsessively monitoring the patient’s status only to be shooed out by Aglaea. She had told him to get some rest and come with a fresh mind tomorrow. How was he even supposed to do that?

He knows Mydei won’t be waiting for him, a pang of guilt stinging his insides just thinking about Mydei waiting for him all afternoon only for him not to show up. Despite that…he still wanted to go to the cafe…wanted to go to a place that made him feel so warm, warm like he was back in his village again before it was razed to the ground. 

His stomach dropped when he saw an unfamiliar grey haired woman manning the counter instead of Mydei, despite logically knowing he wouldn’t be there. He dragged himself to the counter anyway and ordered a lemon bar to go and a glass of water. The grey haired woman stared at him with wide golden eyes—her eyes were not the same warm shade as Mydei's. She didn't even acknowledge his order before violently typing on her phone, muttering holy shit under her breath. Phainon fought back the urge to frown in disapproval. 

His head snapped towards the direction of a door slamming open, his breath hitching when he saw Mydei standing there in a loose white shirt and sleep pants, his hair a wild mess. He was clearly dressed for bed. His golden eyes were wide, his plush mouth open around heaving breaths like he'd run down the stairs. 

“...Phainon, you're here,” he breathed, making his way over to his side. 

“What—” he began and then stopped, as if he could see right through Phainon’s shell of apathy. 

“Are you okay?” He asked, softly. 

Phainon thought of saying he was fine, that he was just late today because of work. But something compelled him to be more honest than he usually would be about things like this.

“I don’t know,” he heard himself say. He felt a warm hand hold his, something that reminded them of their first meeting. 

“Come with me,” Mydei said simply and he followed. 

Mydei lived above his cafe, his apartment also as thoughtfully designed as his workplace—a clean design with a warm rustic finish. He was made to sit down on a soft sage green couch, his host padding towards the kitchen and heating up a tea kettle. Mydei's space felt warm and soft, comfortable despite it being the first time he's ever been here. 

It also smelt like him, like Pomegranates and something heady and warm. His heart thud loudly in his chest, the fact that he was alone in Mydei’s house belatedly hitting him. He hated that he wasn’t mentally all there at the moment, too upset about the patient who never opened their eyes. 

“Drink,” a warm hand cupped his cheek, snapping him out of his rapidly spiraling thoughts. Mydei looked at him with concern, placing the steaming cup of tea on the coffee table. 

“...I won't ask about what happened because you look like you need time…but I can offer you company, if you'd like.” 

He said, sitting beside him on the couch, their shoulders and thighs brushing from the proximity. He wasn't a person who liked to burden people with his worries. He tended to keep things bottled up till it reached a boiling point and exploded. But something about Mydei, something about how worried he looked, how surprised he was when Phainon showed up made him want to spill his guts.

“...I've failed someone,” He heard himself say, his voice cracking and his breath tremulous. There was a heavy feeling in his chest, a lump in his throat that refused to go away. 

“I missed a vital part of an issue during a surgery today and fixed it too late and now the patient won't wake up and—” his breath hitched, tears pricking in his eyes. 

“All these years I've worked so hard to save people and I still couldn't,” he covered his face with his hands, his throat too tight to speak anymore without breaking down. 

A broken noise escaped his lips when he felt careful hands remove his glasses followed by arms wrapping around him and pulling him against a warm chest, a sob tearing its way out of his throat when he felt a hand brushing his hair. 

“It's too early for self-flagellation. I…cannot imagine how you feel at this moment and I will not invalidate your feelings by saying something shallow. But know that I'm here to hold you till you feel like you can save the world again,” Mydei said, his voice gentle and soft and Phainon couldn’t stop the tears that dripped down his cheeks nor could he stop the ugly sobs that wracked his frame. He clutched Mydei’s shirt and sobbed into his chest for what felt like hours, his tears finally petering off into soft shudders of breath when his eyes felt swollen and his temples ached. 

He was also so…so tired. 

“...Stay the night. Sleep beside me…you could use the company,” Mydei murmured. 

He'd somehow managed to maneuver Phainon to his bedroom, made him undress and put on night clothes and then curled up beside him and covered the both of them in a decadently soft duvet. A small noise of surprise escaped him when Mydei pulled him close in an embrace again. He took one of Phainon’s hands in his and placed it on the soft swell of his belly and put his head against his chest. 

Phainon was hit by a severe spell of drowsiness, surrounded by warmth and softness. 

“Wha—” he tried, too tired to actually attempt a protest. 

“...I've heard that cuddling with someone pregnant is supposed to help with stress.” He heard Mydei say, his voice a low rumble. He sounded very, very awkward. 

If Phainon was awake and in a better state of mind he would have definitely teased him about it. But right now, sleep had promptly taken him, his night surprisingly dreamless and warm. 

He snapped awake to the sound of his phone ringing and buzzing on the bedside table. Mydei must have kept it there last night. Speaking of Mydei, he wasn't in bed. Did he already leave for work? He fished his phone out of his pocket and blindly hit the answer button. 

“Hello?” He croaked, clearing his throat right after in mortification. 

“Doctor Phainon!” He heard Castorice say through the receiver, her voice sounding excited despite how crackly it was because of the poor signal. 

“Yeah?” He asked, still half asleep, his eyes trying to droop close even now. 

“The patient, they woke up!” Phainon gasped, sitting up now, fully awake, his heart galloping in his ribcage from his excitement. 

“What?” He said, uncaring of how his voice cracked. 

“Yes! Their recovery has been really smooth.”
